title: QCon London 2026: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond at Monzo
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/shipping-monzo/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773761561765.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Suhail Patel, a principal engineer at Monzo who leads the bank’s platform group, described how the bank has built a developer platform capable of shipping hundreds of changes to production every day.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Managing Asynchronous APIs at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/managing-async-apis/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773756314998.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Ian Cooper, senior principal engineer at Just Eat Takeaway, discussed managing asynchronous APIs in production, showing how endpoint definitions can drive code generation, schema registration, and the automation of messaging infrastructure.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Your Multi-Cloud Strategy Is a Product Problem — Treat It Like One
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/jpmc-multicloud-product-strategy/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773667022672.jpg"/><p>JP Morgan Chase engineers Luis Albinati and Surabhi Mahajan argued that multi-cloud complexity can't be solved with engineering alone. Speaking at QCon London, they showed how treating multi-cloud as a product with capability mapping, demand governance, and defined users tames the chaos.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: AI Is Amplifying Software Engineering Performance, Says the 2025 DORA Report
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/ai-dora-report/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773641593696.jpg"/><p>Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the way software is built, but its impact is more nuanced than many organizations expected. The 2025 DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) report, titled State of AI-Assisted Software Development, finds that AI does not automatically improve software delivery performance.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: QCon London 2026: All Tech Debt is Not Created Equal
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/tech-debt-not-equal/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773696700322.jpg"/><p>Joy Ebertz, Principal Engineer at Imprint, presented at QCon London 2026 a groundbreaking framework for prioritizing technical debt amidst rapid AI-driven code production. By challenging perfectionist mindsets, her six-question approach helps teams assess impact and costs, ensuring focus on vital debt. Jot emphasizes translating tech decisions into financial terms, empowering smarter engineering.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Behind Booking.com's AI Evolution: The Unpolished Story
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/booking-evolution-ai-manuel/en/headerimage/java-istock-image-01-1773724729495.jpg"/><p>Jabez Eliezer Manuel, Senior Principal Engineer at Booking.com, presented “Behind Booking.com's AI Evolution: The Unpolished Story” at QCon London 2026. Manuel discussed how Booking.com has evolved over the past 20 years and the challenges they faced on their journey to incorporate AI.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: Google Open-Sources the Common Expression Language for Python
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/google-cel-expr-python/en/headerimage/google-cel-expr-python-1773686641450.jpeg"/><p>Google has open sourced CEL-expr-python, a Python implementation of the Common Expression Language (CEL), a non-Turing complete embedded policy and expression language designed for simplicity, speed, safety, and portability.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: QCon London 2026: How To Run on Three Clouds at Once, and When Not To
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/form3-triple-active-multicloud/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773663355236.jpg"/><p>Form3 runs UK bank payments across three clouds simultaneously. At QCon London, their engineers explained how they built their custom Kubernetes operators, cross-cloud DNS tricks, and distributed databases, and what happened when they tried to sell them in America. Spoiler: US customers wanted East/West failover, not triple-active multi-cloud.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: QCon London 2026: The Hidden Power of Boring Problems
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/engineering-boring-problems/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773671777267.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Yinka Omole, Lead Software Engineer at Personio, presented a session exploring a recurring dilemma engineers face, whether to spend time mastering the newest technologies and frameworks or to invest in deeper, foundational problems that may appear less exciting but deliver long-term value.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: DoorDash Builds DashCLIP to Align Images, Text, and Queries for Semantic Search Using 32M Labels
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/doordash-semantic-search/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1772917454999.jpg"/><p>DoorDash has launched a multimodal machine learning system that aligns product images, text, and user queries in a shared embedding space. Trained on 32 million labeled query-product pairs using contrastive learning, the system improves semantic search, product ranking, and advertising relevance. Embeddings also support other machine learning tasks across the marketplace.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: Image Processing for Automated Tests
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/image-processing-automated-tests/en/mediumimage/stefan-dirnstorfer-medium-1773150417759.jpg"/><p>Stefan Dirnstorfer discusses the shift from DOM-based testing to visual UI agents. He explains why LLMs often fail at precision tasks - like spotting one-pixel shifts or broken road networks - and shares how advanced image registration and "Chain-of-Thought" vision processing are essential for reliable QA. Learn why combining generative AI with classical algorithms is the future of automation.</p> <i>By Stefan Dirnstorfer</i>

title: Devnexus 2026: Focus on AI with Core Java, Java Frameworks, Security and Career Mentoring
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/devnexus-2026/en/headerimage/java-istock-image-01-1773660621384.jpg"/><p>Celebrating its 23rd year, Devnexus 2026 was held from March 4-6, 2026 at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta, Georgia. The event featured speakers from the Java community who delivered workshops and talks under tracks such as: AI Generative; AI in Practice; Core Java; Java Frameworks; and Security and Developer Tools.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: Article: Evaluating AI Agents in Practice: Benchmarks, Frameworks, and Lessons Learned
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/evaluating-ai-agents-lessons-learned/en/headerimage/evaluating-ai-agents-lessons-learned-header-1773307288872.jpg"/><p>This article introduces practical methods for evaluating AI agents operating in real-world environments. It explains how to combine benchmarks, automated evaluation pipelines, and human review to measure reliability, task success, and multi-step agent behavior. The article also discusses the challenges of evaluating systems that plan, use tools, and operate across multiple interaction turns.</p> <i>By Amit Kumar Padhy</i>

title: Podcast: Andres Almiray on How to Release Any Software to Any OS with JReleaser
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/release-software-jreleaser/en/smallimage/the-infoq-podcast-logo-thumbnail-1773312603825.jpg"/><p>Andres Almiray, a serial open-source contributor and the creator of JReleaser, discusses the project's state, noting that the tool is usable across any ecosystem, not just Java. He also touches on the Common House Foundation's mission.</p> <i>By Andres Almiray</i>

title: Java News Roundup: JHipster 9.0, Project Valhalla, Spring, Helidon, OpenXava, Java Operator SDK
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/java-news-roundup-mar09-2026/en/headerimage/java-istock-image-01-1773563751851.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for March 9th, 2026, features news highlighting: the GA release of JHipster 9.0; Build 27-jep401ea of Project Valhalla; point releases of Spring Tools, Helidon, OpenXava and Java Operator SDK; a maintenance release of Spring Framework; the beta release of the March 2026 edition of Open Liberty; and milestone releases of Micrometer Metrics and Micrometer Tracing.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>
